web_title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan
question: Weighing November's governance, cash-flow, capex, and technical deterioration against the R-32 capacity bull case, should any new capital go into Stallion?

epigraph.quote: Now basically cash flow is not a true reflection of anything.
epigraph.author: Shazad Rustomji, Chairman, CEO and Managing Director, Q2 and H1 FY27 earnings call, 19 November 2026 [36]

web_blocks.html: This chapter weighs both sides of the record and states our final decision. Our verdict is a hard rejection for new capital, down from our 13 November waiting posture. In November 2026, every pillar of the prior hold-and-wait case broke down. Operational KPI health failed, and both flagship plants slipped out of FY27 with cost overruns [36][37][38]. Operating cash flow relapsed to −₹39.17 crore [36]. Monitoring agencies flagged IPO deviation, fund commingling, and unmapped cost-plus-10% EPC advances [37][38]. GST officers cited five tax breaches [39]. The stock broke its 200-day line into Stage 4 at ₹171.59 on 25 November live TradingView, down from ₹180.48 on the 23 November NSE ledger [32]. Our FY28 base value fell to ₹143.2, below both price and the ₹155.07 to ₹159.79 shelf.

web_blocks.title: The strongest honest case for owning Stallion

web_blocks.html: A disciplined bear never attacks a straw man. Stallion still holds a real bull case if execution improves over the next eighteen months. Top-line demand has held up: H1 FY27 revenue grew 19.18% year on year, with Q2 up 28.87% to ₹136.03 crore [14][36]. The 1,200 MTPA Khalapur helium plant began commercial runs on 21 September 2026, opening a path into specialty gases [36][37]. Debt is just ₹7 crore against ₹291.7 crore of September cash and bank balances, avoiding any immediate debt crisis [14][36].

The long-term policy frame also favors domestic capacity. Under the Kigali Amendment, India freezes HFC consumption from 1 January 2028 [17]. Scarcity value tends to rise for firms with working local plants. If Bhilwara's 10,000 MTPA R-32 plant starts cleanly in April–May 2027, Mambattu follows in early FY28, spreads recover, and controls improve, FY28 sales could reach ₹950 crore. That outcome supports an 86% rally to our ₹319.1 bull case.

web_blocks.title: The strongest case against owning Stallion

web_blocks.html: The bear case rests on documented failures from October and November 2026, not speculation. Bhilwara R-32 slipped seven months to May 2027 stabilization with a ₹40 crore overrun and zero upstream AHF integration [36][38]. Mambattu slipped past two prior deadlines into early FY28 with nearly doubled cost scope [36][37]. Both deliver zero FY27 sales. Even before the ₹9.51 crore ESOP catch-up (with ~₹4.7 crore per quarter still ahead in H2), Q2 core operating margin fell 557 bps to 9.19% [36]. In that same quarter, Navin Fluorine, Gujarat Fluorochemicals, and SRF earned 25% to 34% margins behind DGTR's 18 September five-year Chinese R-32 anti-dumping renewal [41][42][43][44].

Cash flow and governance broke together. H1 FY27 operating cash flow fell to −₹39.17 crore despite ₹30.53 crore of pre-tax profit [36]. Meanwhile, ₹129 crore shifted into unmapped cost-plus-10% advances to civil contractor Pansen Engineering before invoicing [38]. CARE Ratings qualified the IPO monitoring report for object deviation, routine-account commingling, misclassified issue costs, and unapproved delays [37]. Infomerics logged ₹36.00 crore (9.9% of gross rights proceeds) spent on issue expenses [38]. In October 2026, Maharashtra GST officers searched the Mumbai office under Section 67 and cited five tax breaches [39]. Stallion paid voluntary tax and interest without disclosing the rupee cost [39].

Insider alignment and candor worsen those flags. Promoter stake dropped 20.10 points in six months, from 67.90% to 47.80% [15][40]. CEO Shazad Rustomji sold 3.06% in the open market in late 2025, then promoters took minimal rights shares [15][40]. Retail ownership crossed 50.3% while institutions fell to 1.88% [15]. After raising ₹524.66 crore in two issues over 14 months, management now signals another ₹200 crore raise [36]. On the 19 November call—with no CFO present—the CEO called ESOP costs not an expense and declared cash flow not a true reflection of anything [36].

web_blocks.takeaway: The bear case now dominates every single pillar—execution, margins, cash conversion, governance, valuation, and technical structure—turning the bull case into an uncompensated long shot.

web_blocks.html: On 13 November, positive FY26 cash flow, an intact 200-day line, and ₹400 crore of March cash kept waiting defensible. Today's record shows aligned failure across quality, cash, controls, and price. No margin of safety remains.

We weight the three FY28 scenarios from chapter 7 based on November's evidence. Given repeated plant slips, negative H1 cash flow, monitoring flags, and coming R-32 oversupply, we set weights at 45% bear, 40% base, and 15% bull. We measure return from the 25 November live TradingView close of ₹171.59 and cross-check against the 23 November NSE ledger close of ₹180.48 [32][36][37][38].

web_blocks.caption: Probability-weighted FY28 equity values per share (11.61 crore base shares, zero surplus FY28 cash) against ₹171.59 live TradingView close [14][32][36]
rows: Red-team stress weighted (15x Bear / 18x Base, debt + ESOP)
web_blocks.takeaway: Expected two-year return is deeply negative (−22.5% headline from ₹171.59 live close; −26.4% from ₹180.48 ledger close) and deteriorates to −43.3% (₹97.4) under the Red-Team debt-interest, ESOP-dilution, and 15x/18x stress audit—reinforcing our hard REJECTED (TIER_0, 0%) posture.

web_blocks.the_number: A headline probability-weighted two-year value of ₹132.9 per share (−22.5% vs ₹171.59; −12.0%/yr; −26.4% vs the 23 November ledger close of ₹180.48), falling to ₹97.4 (−43.3%) under our Red-Team debt-interest and ESOP stress audit.
web_blocks.how_calculated: Each headline case multiplies FY28 net profit by an exit P/E (22x bear, 25x base, 30x bull) with zero surplus cash added, divided by 11.61 crore shares and weighted 45%, 40%, and 15%. The Red-Team stress case charges 10% debt interest (₹15.0 crore post-tax) on ₹200 crore debt, adds 0.16 crore vesting ESOPs (11.77 crore shares), and uses 15x bear / 18x base.
web_blocks.the_inputs: Share count of 11.61 crore base / 11.77 crore ESOP-diluted [14][36]; FY28 sales of ₹500, ₹700, and ₹950 crore at 6.5%, 9.5% (7.36% post-interest), and 13.0% net margins [36][37][38]; multiples discounted below SRF's 32.7x P/E [33].
web_blocks.the_range: At a 15x trough bear P/E alone (₹42.0), weighted value falls to ₹124.1. Equity dilution from a ₹200 crore QIP at ₹150 plus ESOPs (13.10 crore shares) cuts it to ₹117.7 (and Bear at 15x falls to ₹37.2). Combining debt interest, ESOPs, and 15x/18x cuts weighted value to ₹97.4. Even generous 30/45/25 weights yield ₹162.7 (−5.2%).
web_blocks.if_off: To clear our 12.5% yearly hurdle on headline ₹132.9, entry must sit near ₹105.0—and under the ₹97.4 Red-Team stress value, the hurdle entry price drops to ~₹76.9. Both sit far below ₹171.59 and the ₹155.07–₹159.79 diagnostic pivot shelf.

web_blocks.html: Our Red-Team Debt-Interest & ESOP-Dilution Stress Audit confirms that headline math is conservative on downside, not harsh. Charging an assumed 10% pre-tax rate on ₹200 crore of debt (₹15.0 crore post-tax at 25% tax) cuts Base PAT from ₹66.5 crore to ₹51.5 crore (7.36% margin) [1][36]. Adding already-granted one-year-vesting ESOPs (+0.16 crore to 11.77 crore shares) cuts Base value from ₹143.2 to ₹109.4 at 25x (−36.3%) and ₹78.8 at an 18x governance/oversupply multiple (−54.1%) [36]. Replacing Bear's 22x P/E (₹61.6) with 15x yields ₹41.4 (11.77 crore shares) or ₹37.2 (13.10 crore equity-diluted shares). Keeping Bull at 30x (₹314.8 on 11.77 crore shares), probability-weighted value drops from ₹132.9 to ₹97.4 (−43.3%), pulling the 12.5% hurdle re-entry price from ₹105.0 down to ~₹76.9. Every step further reinforces our hard REJECTED (TIER_0, 0%) posture.

This math ends the case for waiting at ₹155.07 to ₹159.79. Even at the top of that diagnostic Pivot S1 shelf, headline Base value (₹143.2) sits 10.4% lower and weighted value (₹132.9) sits 16.8% lower. Reward-to-risk is negative right inside support. Adding 12.9% equity dilution from a ₹200 crore QIP and ESOPs cuts Base to ₹126.9 [36]. Failed KPI health, Stage 4 price action, and negative expected return demand a clean rejection.
We evaluate Stallion separately across short-term trading, medium-term inflection, and long-term compounding as of late November 2026 [32][36][37][38].

Failed governance and cash-conversion KPIs: CARE Ratings IPO deviation/commingling, unmapped cost-plus-10% EPC advances, GST Sec 67 search, 20.1-pt promoter stake drop, and non-AHF exposure to 4x R-32 oversupply [36][37][38][39][40].
web_blocks.takeaway: All three horizons converge on the exact same verdict: reject and stay away until audited execution, positive cash conversion, governance remediation, and a confirmed Stage 2 base replace today's failures.

web_blocks.html: Short-term traders face falling averages and trapped retail supply. Medium-term buyers face zero FY27 plant sales and a ₹200 crore funding gap. Long-term owners cannot back a CEO who dismisses cash flow while compliance breaches pile up. Every horizon calls for zero capital.

Stallion stays rejected until four gates clear together. First, Bhilwara must ship verified commercial R-32 with invoice-mapped EPC closure. Second, operating cash flow must turn positive for two straight quarters with core margins above 14%. Third, monitoring reports and GST compliance must turn clean—including full rupee disclosure of the unquantified October 2026 GST Section 67 settlement in FY27 financial notes and direct CFO-level participation on investor calls—while the ₹200 crore gap closes without heavy equity dilution. Fourth, the stock must build a Stage 1 base and close weekly above its 30-week average (₹202.66) on strong volume.

web_blocks.title: Holding action, capital redeployment, and alert rules

web_blocks.html: Stallion is not held in any account in the 23 November 2026 ledger (total India net worth ₹42.64 lakh; cash ₹14.21 lakh). Zero shares need to be sold, and no stop order is live. Under Tier 0 rejection, new capital allocation stays at zero—both at ₹171.59 and on any drop to ₹155–₹160. All marginal cash stays in cash until another name passes full fundamental, governance, valuation, and Stage 2 checks. We do not force cash into un-underwritten stocks.

The alerts in the decision panel carry zero shares and act strictly as audit prompts, never trade orders. A weekly close below ₹152.41 confirms breakdown toward the ₹130.89 pivot and keeps Stallion discarded. A weekly close back above ₹204.15 on heavy volume—or BSE proof of commercial Bhilwara R-32 dispatches plus clean monitoring reports—triggers a fresh review only.

web_blocks.intro: Position sizing is locked at 0.0% of net worth under Tier 0 rejection. Note that the auto-rendered execution table below references the 2026-11-23 NSE ledger close (₹180.48), while the 2026-11-25 live TradingView close is ₹171.59. The ₹155.07–₹159.79 band and ₹152.41 floor serve purely as diagnostic technical Pivot S1 levels sitting above fundamental Base value (₹143.2), NOT a fundamental buy zone.

web_blocks.html: Holding allocation at zero keeps dry powder ready for genuine Stage 2 leaders with positive cash flow, clean governance, and rising margins. In Indian fluorochemicals alone, integrated peers already deliver those metrics—proving investors need not accept weak controls to own the sector.

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: Changing your call when primary filings turn sour is the job. On 13 November, Stallion looked like a conditional capacity story waiting for a cheaper entry. By 25 November, monitoring-agency flags, unmapped EPC advances, a GST search, negative cash flow, plant slips, a third raise, and a 200-day break ended that thesis.
Capital preservation comes first. Rejecting a broken setup at Tier 0 protects every rupee for managers who respect cash flow and minority owners.

book_paragraphs: Everything we uncovered across the previous eight chapters meets here in one unambiguous verdict: Stallion India Fluorochemicals is a hard rejection for new capital. We are downgrading the company from our 13 November waiting posture to Tier 0 rejected, with zero allocation at today's price and zero intention to catch the stock at its lower support shelf. Before I explain why waiting is no longer defensible, let me lay out both sides of the aisle with total honesty.

Start with the strongest version of the bull case, because dismissing a stock without understanding why optimistic buyers still own it is lazy analysis. Stallion's revenue is still growing: first-half FY27 sales increased 19.2% year on year, with second-quarter revenue rising nearly 29% to 136 crore. The 1,200-tonne Khalapur high-purity helium facility finally commenced commercial operations on 21 September 2026, giving the company a physical foothold in specialty semiconductor and industrial gases. Borrowings sit at just 7 crore against 291.7 crore of September cash and bank balances, so there is no immediate debt crisis. And structurally, India's HFC consumption freeze under the Kigali Amendment starts on 1 January 2028, which could reward domestic producers holding approved refrigerant capacity. If Bhilwara's 10,000-tonne R-32 plant starts smoothly in April and May 2027, Mambattu comes online in early FY28, spreads hold firm, and internal controls improve, FY28 revenue could reach 950 crore and lift the stock to our 319.1 rupee bull case—an 86% gain from 171.59 rupees.

Now put the bear case right next to it, and notice the difference between future hopes and documented facts that arrived in October and November 2026. First, execution broke down across the entire capital programme. Khalapur started 334 days late with standalone helium revenue still undisclosed. Bhilwara R-32 slipped another seven months to March 2027 trials and May stabilization, picking up a 40 crore cost overrun and delivering zero FY27 revenue—while omitting upstream AHF manufacturing in Phase 1. Mambattu slipped past both its October 2025 prospectus date and its August 2026 shareholder-extended deadline into early FY28, also with zero FY27 revenue and nearly doubled cost scope.

Second, underlying profitability weakened precisely when rivals were minting money. Yes, a 9.51 crore two-quarter ESOP catch-up accounted for much of the headline drop to a 2.20% reported operating margin in Q2, and another 4.7 crore per quarter is still coming in the second half. Yet even when you strip out the entire ESOP expense and remove 3.34 crore of treasury other income, core operating profit fell to 12.50 crore—a 9.19% margin, down 557 basis points year on year. In that exact same quarter, Navin Fluorine earned a 34.2% EBITDA margin, Gujarat Fluorochemicals earned 26.9%, and SRF earned a 25.4% Chemicals EBIT margin. Meanwhile, on 18 September 2026, India's trade authority recommended continuing anti-dumping duties on Chinese R-32 for five more years at the request of those integrated peers—squeezing Stallion's China-import blending spreads right as 80,000 tonnes of Indian R-32 supply lines up against 20,000 tonnes of domestic demand.

Third, cash conversion and governance failed together. First-half operating cash flow relapsed to negative 39.17 crore despite 30.53 crore of pre-tax profit, leaving multi-year cumulative operating cash flow deeply underwater. Cash and bank balances shrank by 142 crore in six months while Other Current Assets exploded more than sevenfold to 160.88 crore—chiefly 129 crore of on-account advances to civil contractor Pansen Engineering on a cost-plus-10% contract that Infomerics could not even map to individual invoices. Infomerics also logged 36 crore—nearly ten percent of the gross rights issue—spent on issue expenses. CARE Ratings went further and formally qualified the IPO Monitoring Agency report for deviation from stated objects, commingling of funds across routine bank accounts, prior misclassified issue expenses, and unapproved timeline breaches. And on 15 October 2026, Stallion disclosed a six-day Maharashtra State GST Section 67 search at its Mumbai office that identified five separate Input Tax Credit contraventions, settled through voluntary tax and interest payments whose rupee cost management declined to disclose.

Fourth, insider alignment and management candor raised alarms that no valuation discount can ignore. SEBI SAST filings confirmed that Chairman and CEO Shazad Rustomji sold 24.29 lakh shares—3.06% of the company—in the open market in late 2025, then barely participated in the February 2026 rights issue, cutting promoter ownership by 20.1 percentage points from 67.90% to 47.80% in six months. Institutional ownership collapsed to 1.88% while retail accounts swelled past 50.3%. After raising 524.7 crore across two equity issues in fourteen months, management now signals another 200 crore capital raise—and on the 19 November call, with no CFO present, the CEO dismissed ESOP costs as not an expense and declared that cash flow is not a true reflection of anything. When a CEO tells minority shareholders that operating cash flow means nothing right before asking for a third capital raise, listen carefully and keep your wallet closed.

Putting numbers on those two sides produces an unmistakable expected-return answer. Weighting our re-underwritten FY28 scenarios at 45% bear (61.6 rupees), 40% base (143.2 rupees), and 15% bull (319.1 rupees)—with zero surplus cash added because today's bank balance is already committed to finishing plants and funding working capital—yields a probability-weighted two-year fair value of 132.9 rupees per share. Against the 25 November live TradingView close of 171.59 rupees, that is an expected loss of 22.5%, or negative 12% annualized. Against the 23 November NSE ledger close of 180.48 rupees, it is an expected loss of 26.4%.

Check the sensitivity tests so you know this rejection is not an artifact of one pessimistic assumption. Even if we flip the weights to a generous 30% bear, 45% base, and 25% bull, weighted fair value rises only to 162.7 rupees—still 5.2% below today's price. If the bear case instead trades at a cyclical 15 times trough multiple (42 rupees), weighted value drops to 124.1 rupees. If management fills its signaled 200 crore funding gap with fresh equity at 150 rupees a share alongside the 15.87 lakh ESOP options, diluted share count rises 12.9% to 13.10 crore shares, slashing Base from 143.2 to 126.9 rupees and weighted value to 117.7 rupees. And under our Red-Team debt-interest and ESOP stress audit—charging 10% debt interest (15.0 crore post-tax) to cut Base PAT to 51.5 crore (7.36% margin), counting the 15.87 lakh vesting ESOPs (11.77 crore shares), and using 18 times Base (78.8 rupees; 109.4 at 25 times) and 15 times Bear (41.4 rupees, or 37.2 on 13.10 crore shares)—probability-weighted value drops from 132.9 to 97.4 rupees (−43.3%), pulling the 12.5% hurdle re-entry price from 105.0 down to roughly 76.9 rupees.

That math also explains why we reject Stallion outright rather than parking it in a waiting queue for the 155.07 to 159.79 rupee diagnostic Pivot S1 shelf. At 159.79 rupees, our 143.2 rupee base target sits more than 10% below your entry price, and our 132.9 rupee weighted value sits nearly 17% below it. Reward-to-risk at technical support is negative, while the stock has already broken its 200-day moving average at 183.54 rupees on heavy volume into a confirmed Stage 4 downtrend.

Every holding horizon reaches the same conclusion. For short-term trading and momentum, reject and stay away: price sits under all seven daily and weekly averages with seven recent distribution days, 4-hour RSI at 27.5, and no NSE options chain. For medium-term inflection over six to twenty-four months, reject and stay away: zero FY27 plant revenue, shrinking core spreads, negative operating cash flow, and a 200 crore funding overhang block any clean re-rating. For long-term compounding over three to five years, reject and stay away: failed governance and cash-conversion discipline alongside an unintegrated position in an oversupplied domestic R-32 market disqualify the business as a compounder.

Here is the exact portfolio action. Stallion is not held in any account in our 23 November ledger, so there are zero shares to sell and zero active stops to execute. Position sizing for new capital is locked at 0.0% of net worth under Tier 0 rejection. One hundred percent of the next marginal rupee stays in cash until another business clears every fundamental, governance, valuation, and Stage 2 check. We do not force cash into un-underwritten shortlist or outside names just for the sake of activity.

Could Stallion ever earn its way back onto the radar? Yes, because honest analysis is always open to audited proof—never to promises. It would take four things arriving together: commercial R-32 dispatches and verified invoices from Bhilwara with fixed-cost EPC closure; two consecutive quarters of positive operating cash flow and core operating margins back above 14%; clean monitoring-agency and GST compliance—including full rupee disclosure of the October 2026 GST Section 67 settlement in FY27 financial notes and direct CFO-level participation on investor calls—with transparent resolution of the 200 crore funding gap without punitive dilution; and a completed multi-week Stage 1 base followed by weekly closes back above the 30-week average near 203 rupees on institutional volume. Until every one of those four gates turns green, our capital stays safely on the sidelines.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The hardest discipline in investing is upgrading a wait into a clean rejection when the facts deteriorate instead of clinging to an old support price. When cash flow turns negative, monitoring agencies flag deviations, plants slip again, and the 200-day average breaks, zero percent allocation is the only rational position size.
